title: Sago Palm: Ancient Sago Palms You Can Visit
meta_description: Not a palm at all but a cycad. Sakai's Homesick Cycad, over 1,100 years by tradition, is said to have wept until Oda Nobunaga sent it home.
intro: A sago palm is not a palm at all. Cycas revoluta belongs to the cycads, a lineage that predates flowering plants, largely unchanged since before the dinosaurs, and it grows to match, sometimes a centimetre or two of height a year. Old ones sprawl into colonies of many trunks from one base. Japan names three great cycads. Myokoku-ji's in Sakai is put at over 1,100 years by tradition and Nomanji's at about a thousand, and both carry the same legend: a warlord took the plant to his castle and sent it home after it wept every night for its temple. Ryuge-ji's in Shimizu is one plant with fifty-eight trunks rising from a single base. One beside a museum in Kagoshima carries the name of a discovery: in 1896 a botanist found this species' sperm swimming inside an ovule, the first motile sperm ever seen in a seed plant.
